title: Linear Operational Regime Derivation
purpose: Define the linear operational regime as a derived RT classification selected when orientation-governed continuation is locally composable, role-preserving, and stable under bounded residue influence.

motivation.problem: RT and orientation now support derived regime classification, but the linear regime itself is not yet governed as a derived result.
motivation.resolution: L is registered as a derived regime classification rather than a primitive mathematics floor.

core_definition.L: The linear operational regime derived from RT_core when orientation-governed continuation is locally composable, role-preserving, and stable under bounded residue influence.
core_definition.trace_requirement: Every L-classified regime must constructively trace to RT_core.

derivation_rule.condition: A regime is L-classified iff its oriented continuation admits local composition without residue-induced deformation of the composition rule.

governance_rules.name: Derived Linear Classification
governance_rules.statement: L is a derived regime classification, not a primitive mathematics.

governance_rules.name: Representation Downstream
governance_rules.statement: L may support linear-algebraic representation only after its RT derivation is declared.

governance_rules.name: Composition Failure Conditions
governance_rules.statement: L fails when residue, orientation shift, or admissibility deformation changes the composition rule.

deferred_items: Formal boundary between L and NL
effects: Registers the linear regime as a governed derived classification.
Keeps linear-algebraic representation downstream of RT derivation.
Preserves RT_core as the trace source for L.

notes: Orientation classification remains the governing classifier.
Future nonlinear derivations attach after this linear regime derivation.
The linear regime is derived from RT_core and orientation-governed continuation.
Linear-algebraic representation is permitted only after RT derivation is declared.
This patch is governance and architecture only.
The linear regime is derived from RT_core through orientation-governed classification and does not supersede the canonical root expression.
